video_title: Pump’s Bull Case, Fomo’s Social Moat & Crypto’s Consumer Layer
gist: Blockworks Research analysts (Shondaanda, Carlos) and Average Joe's Crypto (Ryan) argue pump fun has been quietly de-risked — programmatic 50% buybacks since April, a durable ~$6M weekly revenue floor, and a passed July unlock cliff — and debate whether to pair a long with a short in HYPE or Solana. The second half argues FOMO is the breakout consumer app of the cycle, whose moat is its social layer rather than UX or fees, and that the consumer/terminal layer is now the most monetizable layer in crypto.

insights.claim: Pump fun's token has rallied over 100% off its lows while protocol revenue rose roughly 60% over recent weeks, with the rally coming straight through the unlock cliff many investors had feared.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: The move re-rates a token that bears assumed was structurally impaired; the fact that price rose into supply is the setup worth watching.

insights.claim: The two biggest bear arguments against pump fun — team opacity and revenue durability — have been quietly addressed, and the market is only now absorbing that, with the April move to a programmatic buyback-and-burn allocating 50% of revenue removing the discretionary-buyback concern.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Re-rating driver is governance credibility, not new revenue; watch for further IR disclosures as the next leg.

insights.claim: Pump fun has held a weekly revenue floor of $6 million for the past year and recently printed weekly highs near $11 million, undercutting the thesis that memecoin fees are in secular decline.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: A demonstrated revenue floor lets you underwrite a valuation floor; the discount applied for 'fee decay' becomes the mispricing.
insights.quote: it has maintained a weekly floor of $6 million in revenue

insights.claim: Insiders and early investors in pump fun likely hedged or sold OTC well before their tokens unlocked, so monthly unlocks now clear without price impact and the supply overhang has effectively been removed.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Unlocks absorbed without a drawdown is itself a bullish tell; use future monthly unlocks as a live test of remaining seller supply.

insights.claim: An overnight AI agent run over pump fun's on-chain data found no evidence of fraud — bots drive much of the volume, but the revenue and buyback flows appear real rather than circular wash trading.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: The 'pump is faking volume' short thesis is now hard to sustain, since everything needed to falsify it is on chain and auditable.
insights.quote: picture looks very little like crime like everything looks legit

insights.claim: Memecoins are the most durable revenue stream in crypto after stablecoins because a self-contained economy of retail traders keeps trading them regardless of crypto-native sentiment, making the 'pump fun is the OpenSea of this cycle' framing wrong.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: If memecoin fees are annuity-like rather than fad-like, launchpad and terminal cash flows deserve a far lower discount rate than the market applies.
insights.quote: I think meme coins are like the most durable thing in crypto besides stable coins at this point

themes.theme: Cash, hidden expenses and token accrual risk

insights.claim: On-chain data reveals crypto companies' revenue but never their expenses, so pump fun could be paying deployers or traders to route through its platform without any public visibility into Baton Corporation's books.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Treat on-chain revenue as gross, not net; the true cost of customer acquisition is the unmodelable variable across every on-chain business.

insights.claim: For assets with programmatic buybacks, a perfect income statement is unnecessary — if your growth assumptions are right you can model what flows into the token, which is the only asset the holder actually owns.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: A reusable valuation shortcut for opaque crypto issuers: underwrite the mandated flow to the token rather than the enterprise.
insights.quote: for assets that have programmatic buybacks, you don't necessarily need a perfect income statement

insights.claim: A pump fun co-founder recently stated on a podcast that weekly expenses are about $2 million and the foundation holds $2 billion of cash, against a token market cap of roughly $2.3 billion.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Cash approaching the entire market cap means the equity-side option value is enormous — but only if any of it is ever directed at the token.

insights.claim: Pump fun's programmatic buyback commitment only runs one year and its website explicitly states the token is not equity and carries no claims, so nothing yet confirms the token is the value-accrual vehicle — an explicit company statement that it is would trigger a massive re-rating.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: The single highest-convexity catalyst to watch is a formal value-accrual statement or a buyback extension; its absence is the main residual risk.
insights.quote: on the website it explicitly says like pump is not equity. It doesn't represent any claims.

insights.claim: With $2 billion of cash on hand and a trust problem as its number one issue, pump fun should have committed 100% of revenue to buybacks for a year as the cheapest credible signal that the token is a priority.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Frames buyback ratio as a signaling instrument, not a cash-flow decision — a template for judging any token issuer sitting on a large treasury.
insights.quote: It's not like they don't have enough cash, right? Like that would really signal to people that the token is a priority in the long term.

insights.claim: Pump fun's token fell throughout the period when it was buying back 100% of revenue and has rallied since the rate was cut to 50%, which argues the trust deficit was about the growth story rather than the buyback ratio, and that investors may actually reward treasury prudence after watching other crypto companies burn through war chests.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: Empirically undercuts the assumption that maximum buyback equals maximum token performance — a caution for every buyback-driven token thesis.
insights.quote: But they were doing that and the token was down only and now they stopped doing that. The token's going back up.

insights.claim: Pump fun's roughly $100 million a year in operating costs is going largely toward signing traders onto its own trading app, an explicit attempt to compete with FOMO in social trading rather than remain a memecoin launchpad.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: The cut buyback rate is funding a land grab for the consumer layer; success or failure of that app is the swing factor on whether the reallocation was accretive.
insights.quote: their annual cost being like $100 million a year to me is actually like kind of crazy for running like a memecoin launchpad

themes.theme: L1 value chain and the pair trade

insights.claim: Crypto's L1 value chain is separating into three layers — a user layer of trading terminals acting as brokers, a deployer layer that lists assets and takes a cut, and a base layer handling execution — and because front ends abstract the base layer and route to the best venue, base-layer network effects and app enshrinement matter far less than assumed.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Argues capture shifts to user and deployer layers; a reason to underweight L1 tokens relative to the apps routing volume across them.

insights.claim: The rational expression of that framework is long pump fun and short Solana, since Solana trades at a large premium despite generating roughly half pump fun's revenue while the correlation between their revenues is above 0.9.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: A concrete relative-value screen: two highly correlated revenue streams priced at very different multiples.
insights.quote: the correlation between Salana's rev and pump fund revenue is like over.9

insights.claim: Using Solana as the short leg against long pump fun is dangerous because Solana is the casino chip that rips hardest if the on-chain bull case plays out, capping the trade's upside — shorting other L1s expresses the deteriorating-L1-economics view without that correlation.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: Hedge construction matters more than direction here; pick a short leg that does not benefit from your long thesis succeeding.
insights.quote: You don't want to be short the casino chip if there's a gold rush for the casino chip.

insights.claim: HYPE is a sneaky short leg against long pump fun on a flows basis — it is a bear-market darling trading at roughly a 10x higher multiple than pump fun on circulating market cap with declining revenues, and money rotates out of last cycle's winners; Zcash fits the same profile.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: A rotation trade for the start of an on-chain bull: fund new-leadership longs by shorting crowded bear-market outperformers rather than obvious junk.
insights.quote: I do think like hype could be the sneaky short on this

insights.claim: FOMO generated about $3.2 million of revenue in a single recent week, 70% above a record set only one week earlier, extending an eight-week growth streak, and ranked 10th in the US App Store finance charts — evidence it is reaching beyond crypto-native users.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: App Store finance rankings are the cleanest public proxy for net-new retail onboarding into crypto this cycle.
insights.quote: FOMO generated like $3.2 million in revenue last week, which exceeded the previous record set only one week earlier by 70%

insights.claim: FOMO's moat is its social layer rather than its UX or fees, which is why competitors advertising 0% fees and better fills — including pump fun's own trading app — cannot displace it, and why its users trading 100k-200k market cap coins are indifferent to 1% slippage.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: Fee competition is the wrong axis to model in consumer crypto; assess social graph depth instead when valuing terminals.
insights.quote: the value of these apps comes from the social layer and if like you can get actual alpha or insight from just like watching what other people are trading on FOMO. Moving over to another app, you don't get that.

insights.claim: The real bull case for FOMO is that it becomes a social media app built around trading rather than a trading app with social features, in which case its most serious competitor is Robin Hood and its newly launched social product, not pump fun.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: Reframes the comp set from crypto terminals to consumer fintech and social platforms, implying a far larger TAM and a different competitive threat.
insights.quote: the ultimate bullcase for FOMO is it's a social media website built around trading, not a trading app with social media features

insights.claim: If FOMO scales into a mainstream social app it will be forced to implement KYC, because unrestricted no-KYC speculative trading by minors will attract regulatory attention once the user base is large enough to generate news stories.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto
insights.so_what: The main structural risk to the consumer-crypto onboarding thesis is regulatory, and privacy-preserving ZK KYC is the mitigating technology to track.
insights.quote: they they'll have to implement KYC of some sorts

themes.theme: The consumer layer as the monetizable layer

insights.claim: The consumer layer — apps that own users and abstract away infrastructure and cross-chain interoperability — is becoming the most lucrative and monetizable layer in crypto, yet almost none of these revenue-generating trading terminals have a liquid token investors can buy.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Identifies a structural supply gap: the fastest-growing crypto businesses are uninvestable in public markets, forcing capital into imperfect proxies.
insights.quote: It really seems like that consumer layer is becoming the most lucrative and most monetizable layer to build on

insights.claim: Pump fun is the closest available liquid proxy for FOMO's success because FOMO has neither a token nor accessible equity, while most coins traded on FOMO originate from pump fun.
insights.speaker: Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: A directly actionable way to express the FOMO growth story in liquid markets today.

insights.claim: Roughly 40 to 50% of FOMO's recent revenue comes from the relay side, making it a leading bridge business almost as a byproduct of building a chain-agnostic trading app where users can deposit from and withdraw to any chain.
insights.speaker: host and Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: Interop revenue accrues to whoever owns the user, not to dedicated bridge protocols — bearish for standalone bridge tokens.
insights.quote: 40 to 50% in recent weeks coming from the relay side

insights.claim: FOMO launching its own token launchpad would be mission creep that undermines its ambition to be the social layer for all trading, though the mirror-image scenario is the main bear case for pump fun — analogous to how pump fun's own PumpSwap AMM stopped graduating tokens to Radium and crushed Radium's forward revenue in early 2025.
insights.speaker: Ryan, Average Joe's Crypto and Carlos, Blockworks Research
insights.so_what: The Radium precedent shows how fast an upstream player can vertically integrate and destroy a downstream token's revenue — the key tail risk to a long pump fun position.
insights.quote: if FOMO employees are listening to this, please do not launch a launchpad
